macro_events.resolution: 2 consecutive negative GDP quarters (BEA) or NBER declaration by Q4 2026 advance estimate
macro_events.mar_relevance: Direct demand risk — recession would reduce business/leisure travel spending, lower RevPAR and occupancy across MAR portfolio

macro_events.resolution: Advance Estimate for Q4 2026 from BEA reports full-year 2026 GDP growth below 0%
macro_events.mar_relevance: Negative full-year GDP would be severe for lodging — implies sustained demand destruction beyond cyclical dip

macro_events.resolution: Upper bound of target federal funds rate increased at any point between Jan 1, 2026 and Dec 2026 FOMC meeting
macro_events.mar_relevance: Rate hike would increase MAR's debt servicing costs (~$12B long-term debt) and potentially dampen travel demand via macro tightening

macro_events.event: US inflation >3% at any point in 2026
macro_events.resolution: BLS CPI-U YoY exceeds 3% for any month in 2026
macro_events.mar_relevance: Elevated inflation supports MAR's pricing power (room rates adjust with CPI) but compresses consumer discretionary budgets; net effect depends on wage growth lag

macro_events.event: Number of Fed rate cuts in 2026
macro_events.resolution: Count of 25bps rate cuts by Dec 31, 2026
macro_events.note: Kalshi market active but specific bracket probabilities not retrievable via search. Jan 2026 FOMC: 99% predicted hold. Market split on full-year cut count.
macro_events.mar_relevance: Rate cuts would reduce MAR's financing costs and stimulate travel demand; consensus uncertain on magnitude

macro_events.resolution: BLS Employment Situation report for February 2026
macro_events.mar_relevance: Unemployment 4.2-4.4% range (84% combined) suggests stable labor market — supportive for business travel and group bookings but not overheating

industry_events.resolution: WHO declares any disease a pandemic between Jan 1 and Dec 31, 2026
industry_events.note: Market exists but current probability not retrievable via search. COVID-19 devastated hotel industry (MAR RevPAR -60% in 2020) — tail risk for lodging sector
industry_events.mar_relevance: Pandemic tail risk — MAR's asset-light model proved more resilient than owned-hotel peers in COVID but still saw massive RevPAR decline

industry_events.event: 100% tariff on Canada in effect by June 30, 2026
industry_events.resolution: General 100% tariff rate on Canadian imports goes into effect by June 30, 2026
industry_events.mar_relevance: Extreme Canada tariffs would dampen cross-border travel and Canadian outbound tourism to US (Canada is top-3 international source market for US hotels)

industry_events.event: US tariff rate on China — March 31, 2026 distribution
industry_events.resolution: US tariff rate on Chinese imports as of March 31, 2026
industry_events.mar_relevance: China tariffs affect Chinese outbound tourism to US (visa/sentiment) and broader trade war escalation risk that could trigger recession scenario

industry_events.event: 10% US blanket tariff in effect on March 31, 2026
industry_events.resolution: Whether a 10% blanket tariff on all US imports remains in effect on March 31, 2026
industry_events.mar_relevance: Blanket tariff raises costs across economy (construction materials for hotel development, FF&E) and dampens international goodwill toward US travel

industry_events.resolution: Official US-China trade agreement reached before July 2026
industry_events.note: Market resolved Yes — US-China temporary trade deal already in place (Aug 2025 90-day extension). Current tariff level 15-25% most likely.
industry_events.mar_relevance: Trade deal stability reduces downside tail risk for Chinese tourism to US and general macro uncertainty

synthesis.macro_regime: Market consensus leans mildly cautious: 23.5% recession risk (elevated but not dominant), 67% chance inflation exceeds 3% (tariff-driven), 93% blanket tariff persists. Rate hike risk low (10%). Unemployment stable around 4.3%.

mar_implications.base_case: Moderate growth with inflation — supports RevPAR growth via pricing power but margin pressure from wage/cost inflation. Stable employment supports business travel.
mar_implications.bull_scenario: No recession + rate cuts + trade normalization → strong leisure/business recovery, international inbound tourism rebounds
mar_implications.bear_scenario: Recession (23.5%) + tariff escalation → RevPAR declines 5-15%, group cancellations, international tourism freeze. 100% Canada tariff (10%) would specifically hit cross-border demand.
mar_implications.key_monitoring: Watch recession probability trajectory (currently 23.5%), tariff escalation path, and monthly unemployment prints above 4.5%
